title: Digital ICs and logic gates
blurb: Explain comparators, gate symbols, logic families, tri-state outputs, pull resistors and how FPGAs are designed.

E6C01.why: Hysteresis uses separate rising and falling thresholds, so **noise can't make the output chatter**.

E6C02.why: A comparator's whole job: when the input crosses the threshold, the **output changes state**.
E6C02.trap: The output is a logic level, not a copy of the reference.

E6C03.why: Tri-state means outputs of **0, 1 and high impedance** (effectively disconnected).
E6C03.trap: Nothing to do with ternary math or impedance matching.

E6C04.why: BiCMOS combines **CMOS's high input impedance with bipolar's low output impedance**.
E6C04.trap: It is not simpler or cheaper, and still needs static precautions.

E6C05.why: CMOS draws almost no current except when switching: the **lowest power**.
E6C05.trap: ECL is fast, but it draws a lot of power.

E6C06.why: A threshold near **half the supply** leaves a wide margin either side, so noise rarely flips the input.
E6C06.trap: A threshold above the supply could never switch.

E6C07.why: A pull-up or pull-down ties a line to the supply or ground, **setting a defined voltage** when nothing drives it.
E6C07.trap: Key-click and oscillator drift need different parts.

E6C08.why: A flat-backed AND shape with an inversion bubble on the output is a **NAND**.
E6C08.trap: The same shape without the bubble is AND.

E6C09.why: FPGAs are configured by describing the logic in a **hardware description language** such as VHDL or Verilog.
E6C09.trap: Karnaugh maps help simplify logic by hand; they don't configure the chip.

E6C10.why: A curved-back OR shape with an inversion bubble on the output is a **NOR**.
E6C10.trap: Without the bubble it is OR; flat-backed with a bubble is NAND.

E6C11.why: A plain triangle with a bubble is the **NOT** (inverter): one input, output opposite.
E6C11.trap: Two-input shapes are AND, OR, NAND or NOR.
